claims.text: The starting refractory HEA powder is an equimolar mixture of W, Nb, Mo, Ta, and V.
The elemental powders have 99.5% purity.
Ball milling, spray granulation with 2.5 wt.% starch, and radiofrequency-plasma spheronization produce a spherical WNbMoTaV RHEA powder suitable for cladding.
Laser cladding a 2 mm preset WNbMoTaV layer onto TC4 at approximately 3.5 kW creates a dense, fine-grained coating.
The coating is metallurgically bonded to the TC4 substrate.
The coating primarily contains a high-strength BCC solid solution.
The coating contains a secondary Ti-rich phase.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding produces the refined coating microstructure.
A laser power near 3.5 kW optimally balances complete powder melting against dilution by the TC4 substrate.
Lattice distortion in the BCC solid solution increases coating hardness.
Solid-solution strengthening increases coating hardness.
Fine grains increase hardness through grain-boundary strengthening.
A partial protective tribo-oxide layer forms during sliding wear.
The tribo-oxide layer limits plowing and reduces wear volume.
The coating produced near 3.5 kW will have significantly greater Vickers microhardness than bare TC4.
The coating produced near 3.5 kW will have significantly lower wear volume than bare TC4 under the specified reciprocating-wear conditions.
Bare TC4 has an average microhardness of 341.25 HV0.3.
Bare TC4 has a wear-volume loss of 6.09 × 10^7 μm³ under the stated wear conditions.
Laser powers of 3.1 and 3.9 kW were previously found to be less effective than powers near 3.5 kW.
Quantitative hardness and wear improvements vary with laser power, powder morphology, and substrate dilution.

contradictions.description: The proposed coating measurements use a 0.98 N Vickers load, corresponding approximately to HV0.1, whereas the stated baseline is reported as HV0.3, corresponding to about 2.94 N. Thus, the assertion that hardness is compared under identical conditions is inconsistent unless the baseline is remeasured at 0.98 N or the coating is also measured at HV0.3.
